top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
top_sast_rules.description: Leaking information about an exception, such as messages and stack traces, to an external user can expose implementation details that are useful to an attacker for developing a subsequent exploit.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-497. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
top_sast_rules.description: Logging sensitive information without encryption or hashing can expose it to an attacker.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-359. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
top_sast_rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find code that may expose sensitive information in error messages, logs, or responses
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper access controls. Use generic error messages for users. Avoid exposing sensitive information in error responses, debugging output, or log files.

top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove dead code through static analysis. Use code coverage tools to identify unreachable code. Implement regular code reviews to eliminate unused functionality.

top_sast_rules.description: An access-control policy is missing or incorrectly enforced for a protected resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-284 access-control authorization permission acl role owner ownership privilege protected-resource protected-endpoint allow deny
top_sast_rules.remediation: Require explicit server-side authorization before protected operations.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
top_sast_rules.description: A protected resource crosses its intended trust or control boundary and becomes accessible to an unintended actor.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-668 wrong-sphere control-sphere trust-boundary resource-exposure unintended-actor private-resource public-exposure insecure-permission cross-boundary
top_sast_rules.remediation: Keep protected resources inside their intended trust boundary.

top_sast_rules.description: An authorization check exists but evaluates access incorrectly.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-863 incorrect-authorization authorization-check permission-check role-check ownership-check acl-check access-decision bypass
top_sast_rules.remediation: Evaluate authorization from trusted server-side identity and policy state.

top_sast_rules.description: Legacy access-control category for failures in permissions, privileges, or authorization enforcement.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-264 permissions privileges access-control authorization acl role privilege owner permission enforcement
top_sast_rules.remediation: Enforce trusted authorization, role, ownership, and permission checks.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Files
top_sast_rules.description: Sensitive information is written to debug or diagnostic log files.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-534 debug-log diagnostic-log verbose-log sensitive-log password token credential secret exception stacktrace logging
top_sast_rules.remediation: Redact secrets and disable sensitive diagnostic logging.

top_sast_rules.description: Disabling or weakening CSRF protection may make the application vulnerable to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attack.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find state-changing operations that lack CSRF protection mechanisms
